relevance_note: Single-patient case report with individual-level detail: "A 7-year-old male patient with Alexander’s disease"; no GFAP variant is printed or tied to him.
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcription by script (script only assembled JSON). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No variants row: the paper states only that Alexander's disease is in general caused by a GFAP mutation and never says the patient was genetically tested or carries a specific GFAP variant, so no variant is tied to him; clinical_diagnosis_basis left not reported for the same reason. Age 7 is recorded as age at last evaluation (age at the reported procedure); 18 months is age at diagnosis; onset not stated (features were 'presented' at diagnosis, so onset left null). The Table lists anesthetic procedures (rows are procedures, not people); no phenotype data in it. Hypotensive episodes occurred during anesthesia in earlier procedures; the paper says 'no significant hypotension was noted in this EEG-guided procedure' (procedure-specific, not recorded as excluded; not a contradiction). Intraoperative hypotension not mapped to the autonomic-dysfunction checklist item. The authors' hedged interpretation of 'increased sensitivity to propofol' was not recorded as a feature. Macrocephaly/seizures/developmental delay in the Introduction are general disease statements, not about this patient. Vital status not explicitly stated.
